title: 12/01 — Academic context terms (the §3.5 context check's vocabulary)
consumer: P6 Task 10 (src/facts/rules.py, injected — never module-level per the P6 plan's injection discipline) and CONNECTION.md section 4 step 1, where deterministic activation evaluates pattern-plus-context rules of exactly this shape. The terms are matched against the P4 `context_before` / `context_after` window around a course-code-shaped candidate.
match_field: the surrounding-context window of an observation (P4 `surrounding context`), never the candidate value itself. A context term is context: it is not a value, it fills no field, and it never produces a fact of its own.
normalization_for_matching: case-insensitive (P6 SPEC N-6: the §3.5 context check matches a term regardless of the case it appears in) AND word-boundary (P6 SPEC: a case-insensitive match is not a substring match, so `semester` must not match inside a longer word). Multi-word terms match as a contiguous word-bounded phrase inside one text unit; a phrase never matches across a sentence-terminating punctuation mark, so "...the problem. Set aside..." does not contain the term "problem set".
field_key_note: The fact these terms gate is the academic field whose ratified stored key is `subject` (D6, ratified 2026-08-21, recorded in _CONTRACT.md rule 8 and DECISION-BRIEF.md). `course` is the design's prose name for the same concept and survives inside quotations only. The adversarial fixture A03 spells the field `course`; it predates the ratification and is cited here as an acceptance constraint on values, not on the key.

design_cites.quote: BUSIB 4300 becomes a course fact only when the engine finds a course-code pattern together with academic context such as “syllabus,” “lecture,” “credits,” “instructor,” or “semester.”
A validated fact was found by a deterministic rule and passed contextual checks, such as a course-code pattern appearing beside “lecture,” “syllabus,” or “semester.”
It should use word-boundary matching rather than substring matching.

rules: **The floor is design and closed against removal.** The five floor terms are the design's own list and are required. P6's plan treats the list as required-and-extensible (PLAN-SKELETON Task 10, injected; its D5 note reads the design's 'such as' as a floor, not a closed set). Removing or weakening a floor term is editing the design.

**Extensions are proposal and never alone.** Every non-floor term carries `never_alone: true`: an extension term by itself never satisfies the §3.5 context check. It contributes only when a floor term is also present in the window, or under the injected `extension_context_policy` slot (which combinations of extension terms, if any, suffice without a floor term — a policy Joseph sets; this file states no policy).

**A context term fills no field.** Several floor and extension terms are also plausible *values* of the deferred `work_type` enum (syllabus, lecture, homework, midterm, problem set). That enum is a separate deferred item (P6 SPEC Deferred: allowed value sets for enum-like fields) and is not authored here. This file authors context duty only.

**Word boundaries survive case-insensitivity.** `accredits` does not satisfy `credits`; `lecturer` does not satisfy `lecture`; `semesterly` does not satisfy `semester`. This is the same discipline that keeps `MIT` out of "submit" and `UNC` out of "uncertainty" (A01, A02).
**No numbers.** No term carries a weight, score, distance, or window size. The context-window extent is P4's; every threshold downstream is an injected slot.

entries.variants_provenance: inference — plural inflections of the design literal; the literal alone misses "all syllabi are posted"

false_friend.description: A United States Supreme Court opinion opens with a section titled Syllabus (a headnote, prepared by the Reporter of Decisions). A downloaded court opinion PDF therefore contains the floor term while being a legal document, not coursework. The course-code pattern requirement carries the defense: a court syllabus has no co-occurring course-code-shaped candidate.
false_friend.example_false: SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES — Syllabus — No. 22-451

entries.rationale: First of the design's five literals, and the strongest: the design's own walking fixture is the filename Syllabus BUSIB 4300 Spring 2026.pdf. P4's skeleton fixture 1 carries `context_before: "Syllabus — "` with a capital S, which is why the check is case-insensitive (P6 SPEC N-6, B8(a)).

entries.variants_provenance: inference — the plural appears in real course material ("all lectures are recorded") and the design's own grouping example is the file Lecture 08.pdf

false_friend.description: Public lecture series (museums, TED-style events) and the scolding sense ("got a lecture about it") use the same word outside coursework. `lecturer` does not match — word boundary — even though a lecturer is academic; adding `lecturer` is an open extension question (see uncertain).

entries.variants_provenance: inference — real syllabi write "3 credit hours" and "credit" in the singular; the bare singular is riskier (credit card, credit score) and is listed as a variant for Joseph's review, not asserted

false_friend.description: The highest false-friend load on the floor: film and game closing credits, account credits, tax credits (a Form 1040 mentions child tax credits), and credit-card statements all carry the word. The defense is structural: the term is only consulted when a course-code-shaped candidate exists, and catalogue 02's stoplist keeps FORM 1040 from being that candidate.
false_friend.example_false: closing credits roll at the end of the film

entries.rationale: Third design literal. Kept at floor strength because the design puts it there; the false-friend load is documented, not used to demote it.

false_friend.description: Driving instructor, fitness instructor, flight instructor, ski instructor: the word names a role in many non-academic services. A driving-school receipt with an invoice number shaped like a course code is the realistic collision; catalogue 02's shape limits and §3.7's margin carry the defense.
false_friend.example_false: your driving instructor will meet you at the DMV

false_friend.description: The safest floor term: essentially all uses are academic. Residual risk is metaphorical ("a semester's worth of drama") and German loan contexts where Semester is also the standard word (which is a hit, not a false friend).

entries.variants_provenance: proposal — non-standard plural common in course sites

false_friend.description: Daft Punk's 1997 album is titled Homework — a tagged music file or a review carries the word with no coursework anywhere. Business idiom "do your homework" appears in due-diligence documents. Both are why this term is never_alone.

entries.rationale: The design's own worked sparse file is HW 3.pdf whose content says only equations and the phrase Homework 3 — the word marks homework-ness (a work-type clue), not a course. As context it may support a course-code candidate elsewhere in the window, but never alone.
entries.quote: A file named HW 3.pdf may contain only equations and the phrase “Homework 3,”

entries.variants_provenance: proposal — plural and hyphenated forms both occur

false_friend.description: Midterm elections. A saved news article "2026 midterm election forecast" carries the word beside plenty of four-digit numbers. never_alone plus the course-code shape (an election year is a bare year, which catalogue 02 refuses as a course and catalogue 04 refuses as a date) carries the defense.

entries.rationale: Midterm Practice.pdf is one of the design's grouping-example course files, so the word is real course vocabulary; the election sense is why it cannot be floor.

entries.variants_provenance: proposal — `pset` is live student vocabulary (MIT and elsewhere) but is also a Unix ps flag-ish token; kept as a variant for review

false_friend.description: Two hazards. (1) The phrase must not be assembled across a sentence boundary: "...describes the problem. Set aside an hour..." contains `problem` and `set` but not the term — the phrase-matching rule above forbids it. (2) Chess problem sets and competitive-programming contest problem sets are genuinely problem sets that are not university coursework; never_alone keeps them from validating a course on their own.
false_friend.example_false: we understood the problem. Set the timer and begin

entries.rationale: Problem Set 2.pdf and Problem Set 4.pdf are the design's own grouping-example filenames; the phrase is core course vocabulary.

false_friend.description: Every business, clinic, and government office publishes office hours. A dentist's appointment letter ("our office hours are 9–5") is the everyday collision, and such letters carry reference numbers shaped like course codes more often than syllabi do. Firmly never_alone.
false_friend.example_false: our office hours are Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm

entries.rationale: Standard syllabus vocabulary (instructor office hours) — but the phrase alone is closer to a business-document signal than an academic one.
entries.design_cite: 00 §3.5 (extension of the floor; the design's list is introduced with 'such as')

false_friend.description: Three-way ambiguity, named in the dispatch: Canvas the LMS (Instructure) vs canvas the painting surface vs canvas the material/product (canvas tote, canvas print) — plus the HTML canvas element in web-dev material. An art-supply receipt or a frontend tutorial carries the word with zero academic meaning. Case is no help (sentence-initial Canvas vs the brand). Firmly never_alone; even beside a floor term it should stay the weakest supporter.

entries.rationale: "submitted on Canvas" / "see Canvas for the rubric" is ubiquitous real coursework context in LMS-era corpora — too valuable to omit, too ambiguous to trust alone.
entries.example_true: Upload your problem set to Canvas by 11:59pm

false_friend.description: Blackboard the LMS (Anthology) vs the physical blackboard. The physical sense shows up exactly where this product looks: OCR of classroom photos and whiteboard/blackboard captures — the design itself lists whiteboards among dense-text photo subjects. A photo caption "equations on the blackboard" is photographic context, not LMS context.
false_friend.example_false: chalk dust on the old blackboard

entries.rationale: Same LMS logic as canvas: high-value institutional context in real corpora, unusable alone.
entries.example_true: Grades are posted on Blackboard for ECON 1001

refused.rationale: A university name is a gazetteer value (R4's content), not a context term. The design is explicit that the name alone is ambiguous across roles, which is exactly why it cannot serve as the §3.5 context that validates a course fact: it would launder the ambiguity into a validation.
refused.quote: A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.
refused.example_false: Columbia 4300 (no course fact: 'Columbia' is not a context term)

refused.term: numbers, section marks, or dates as context
refused.rationale: A nearby year, date, or section number is not academic context. The design's date discipline exists because year-shaped numbers are routinely course identifiers, versions, builds, and ZIP codes; letting one number validate another would be circular.

refused.term: school, university, college, class, course (the bare words)
refused.rationale: Too broad to gate anything: "school of thought", "a class of problems", "of course", "collision course", "university district" all defeat word-boundary matching semantically while passing it lexically. `course` in particular appears in ordinary prose at a rate that would make the §3.5 check meaningless. Any of these becoming context terms needs corpus evidence and Joseph's sign-off.
refused.example_false: of course, the collision course continued

uncertain.term: exam, quiz, assignment, tutorial, professor, prerequisite, lecturer, transcript, GPA
uncertain.rationale: Each is plausible academic context and each has a real hazard: exam (medical exam, eye exam), quiz (pub quiz, marketing quizzes), assignment (legal assignment of rights, work assignments), tutorial (software tutorials — enormous false-friend load in a developer corpus), professor (form of address in journalism), prerequisite (business/legal prose), lecturer (job-title zone overlap with instructor), transcript (P4 has a `transcript` zone for audio/video captions — the word collides with the product's own vocabulary), GPA (safe but rare outside transcripts). None is authored; each would be `proposal` + never_alone if Joseph wants it.

uncertain.term: CJK context-term slot (学期, 講義, シラバス, 単位, 学分, 수업, 학기 …)
uncertain.rationale: The design requires CJK support in extraction — the OCR section's own words are that Apple Vision needs “appropriate language support including CJK where required” — so the context-term list will eventually need CJK members (学期 semester zh/ja, 講義 lecture ja, シラバス syllabus ja, 単位 credits ja, 学分 credits zh, 학기 semester ko). They are recorded here as a named slot (`cjk_context_terms_slot`) rather than as entries because (a) word-boundary matching is Latin-script machinery and CJK needs its own boundary rule, and (b) this list should be verified by a native reader against a real corpus before it gates fact creation. Nothing here is authored as active.

Whether some combination of extension terms with no floor term can ever satisfy the §3.5 check (e.g., `homework` + `midterm` + `office hours` all in one window) is a policy fork, not data. The slot is named; the policy is Joseph's. Until set, the safe reading is: extensions support only in the presence of a floor term.

acceptance_fixtures: tests/eval/fixtures/adversarial/A01.json — `MIT` inside "submit" must produce nothing; the word-boundary rule here is the same rule that protects it
tests/eval/fixtures/adversarial/A03.json — a course-code-shaped ZIP or device model must abstain; context terms are half of that defense (catalogue 02 is the other half)
sourcing_note: The floor is sourced to the design alone. Extension terms and false friends are authored from common knowledge of coursework and LMS vocabulary (Canvas/Instructure, Blackboard/Anthology, Daft Punk's Homework, US midterm elections, Supreme Court syllabi) — none required external verification beyond RESEARCH.md's notes.
